stem: A tennis ball is released from a height ‘h’ and it rebounds to a height ‘h/2’ after hitting the floor. Which of the following graphs best represent the velocity-height of the ball?

assets.alt: Velocity v against height h: from height h at zero velocity, a large loop below the axis reaches the origin with negative velocity; then a small loop above the axis goes up to height h/2 and back, drawn as circular arcs.

Velocity v against height h: from height h, a curve below the axis bends steeply down to a large negative velocity near the origin; after the bounce, a short curve above the axis falls from a small positive velocity to zero at h/2, both concave towards the axes.

Velocity v against height h: a straight line below the axis from zero at height h to a large negative velocity at the origin; after the bounce, a straight line above the axis from a positive velocity at the origin down to zero at h/2.

Velocity v against height h: a parabolic curve below the axis from zero at height h to a large negative velocity at the origin; after the bounce, a smaller parabolic curve above the axis from a positive velocity at the origin to zero at h/2.

Graph of velocity against height y. Falling from h, v is negative and grows to its largest size at the ground. After the bounce, v is positive and falls to zero at h/2. The curves have vertical tangents where v = 0, at h and h/2.
